messages.content: Hi, welcome. I'm glad you're here. How are you feeling today?
Uh, okay. I guess I'm fine. Just... here.
It sounds like you're not quite sure how you're feeling. Could you tell me a little more about what "just... here" is like for you right now?
I don't know, it's just... I'm sitting here, but my mind is kind of blank. Like I'm going through the motions. I guess I feel a little out of place.
That sense of being out of place and going through the motions—can you tell me what’s been happening in your life that might be connected to feeling that way?

Well, I mean... it's nothing big. Just work, mostly. The assembly line, you know? It's the same thing every day. And then I go home and... I don't know. I see my roommate going out with friends, trying new restaurants, and I just... I make my mac and cheese. It's stupid, but it makes me feel like I'm stuck. Like I'm just this boring guy in a loop.

patient_profile.presenting_problem:
I feel like I am boring and lame because I love Mac and cheese, which affects my self-perception and self-esteem.
These feelings of being boring started about a year ago.
I believe the cause of this issue is societal judgment and media influence on what is considered interesting or cool.
The problem has progressed to the point where I avoid socializing or trying new activities because I feel inadequate.
I experience these feelings whenever I eat Mac and cheese or when I see others enjoying different, more diverse foods.
I have attempted to try new foods and engage in different activities to break this cycle but have not succeeded.
patient_profile.reason_seeking_counseling: I decided to seek counseling because I noticed that my feelings of inadequacy were limiting my social interactions and overall enjoyment of life.
patterns: black-and-white or polarized thinking / all or nothing thinking

more_information.past_history:
(including medical history)
I have not experienced similar problems before.
I have not received treatment or counseling for psychological issues previously.
I do not have any significant physical illnesses.
more_information.social_support_system: I have a roommate whom I can talk to about everyday matters but do not feel comfortable discussing my feelings of inadequacy with them.
